record.paper_title: Vector bundles on curves and generalized theta functions: recent results and open problems
record.original_question: As the curve X varies in the moduli space M_g of smooth genus-g curves, the spaces H^0(SU_X(r), L^k) form a flat projective bundle and therefore define a projective representation ρ_{r,k}: Γ_g → PGL(H^0(SU_X(r), L^k)) of the mapping class group Γ_g = π_1(M_g, X). What is this representation ρ_{r,k}?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a smooth complex projective curve of genus $g\ge 2$, and let $\mathrm{SU}_X(r)$ denote the moduli space of semistable rank-$r$ vector bundles on $X$ with trivial determinant. Let $\mathcal{L}$ be the ample generator of $\mathrm{Pic}(\mathrm{SU}_X(r))\cong\mathbb{Z}$ (the determinant line bundle). For each integer $k\ge 1$, consider the finite-dimensional vector space of generalized theta functions
$$V_{r,k}(X) := H^0(\mathrm{SU}_X(r),\mathcal{L}^{\otimes k}).$$

As $X$ varies over the moduli space $\mathcal{M}_g$ of smooth genus-$g$ curves, the spaces $V_{r,k}(X)$ assemble into a holomorphic vector bundle on $\mathcal{M}_g$ (or on Teichmüller space $\mathcal{T}_g$) that carries a canonical projectively flat connection (the Hitchin connection). Projectivizing the resulting monodromy yields a projective representation of the mapping class group $\Gamma_g = \pi_1(\mathcal{M}_g, X)$:
$$\rho_{r,k}: \Gamma_g \longrightarrow \mathrm{PGL}(V_{r,k}(X)).$$

Identify the projective representation $\rho_{r,k}$. More precisely, give an intrinsic topological/algebraic description of $\rho_{r,k}$ (for example, in terms of a known modular functor or topological quantum field theory), and describe its image, kernel, and characters.
artifact.category_tag: Moduli of vector bundles and conformal blocks
artifact.status_search_result: The representation $\rho_{r,k}$ has been identified, via the Hitchin connection and its identification with the WZW/TUY connection on conformal blocks, with the $\mathrm{SU}(r)$ Reshetikhin–Turaev (Witten) TQFT projective representation of the mapping class group. This identification was completed by Laszlo (matching Hitchin and TUY connections) and by Andersen–Ueno (equivalence of the conformal-blocks modular functor with the skein/Reshetikhin–Turaev modular functor for $\mathrm{SU}(n)$). However, finer structural questions about $\rho_{r,k}$ — its kernel (asymptotic faithfulness is known, by Andersen, but the precise kernel for fixed $k$ is not), the image, irreducibility, and a complete intrinsic character formula — remain only partially understood.

status_evidence.title: Construction of the Witten–Reshetikhin–Turaev TQFT from conformal field theory (Andersen–Ueno)
status_evidence.snippet: Andersen and Ueno provide an explicit isomorphism from the modular functor underlying the skein-theoretic model for the Witten–Reshetikhin–Turaev TQFT to the vacua modular functor.
status_evidence.claim: The conformal-blocks (vacua) modular functor for SU(n) is isomorphic to the Reshetikhin–Turaev modular functor, identifying the corresponding mapping class group representations.

status_evidence.title: On modular functors (Henriques)
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of subtleties in the Andersen–Ueno identification of modular functors.
status_evidence.claim: Some technical aspects of the equivalence between the two modular functors have been disputed, indicating the identification is not entirely settled in full generality.

status_evidence.title: Asymptotic properties of the Hitchin–Witten connection
status_evidence.snippet: Studies asymptotic faithfulness and related properties of the quantum representations from the Hitchin connection.
status_evidence.claim: Properties such as asymptotic faithfulness of $\rho_{r,k}$ are known, but a complete description of kernel/image for fixed $k$ remains open.
